title: A 10M IOPS Kioxia GP1 SSD Shown Running at FMS 2026
gist: Kioxia demonstrated a live GP1 Series enterprise NVMe SSD sustaining just over 10 million random read IOPS, built on PCIe Gen6 and second-generation XL-FLASH SLC-class NAND, with a stated industry goal of reaching 100M IOPS drives within roughly a year. The drive targets a new ultra-fast storage tier for AI servers that offloads some traditional DRAM tasks to lower-cost NAND, a performance-first play in an otherwise capacity-constrained flash market.

insights.claim: Kioxia's GP1 Series enterprise NVMe SSD claims up to 10 million random read IOPS per drive at a 512-byte block size, with an endurance rating up to 50 DWPD.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: A 10M IOPS / 50 DWPD single drive resets the spec bar for enterprise flash and gives Kioxia a differentiated high-margin SKU outside the commodity capacity race.
insights.quote: Kioxia claims up to 10 million random read IOPS per drive at a 512-byte block size, plus an endurance rating up to 50 DWPD.
insights.locator: Kioxia Shows off its 10M IOPS GP1 SSD

insights.claim: Kioxia ran the 10M IOPS GP1 drive live on the show floor rather than showing a static slide, with output so steady that observers initially mistook the live dashboard for a rendered slide.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: A live, stable demo rather than a datasheet claim signals the product is near-productizable, shortening the gap between announcement and revenue.
insights.quote: with performance so consistent that we originally thought it was just a static slide rather than a live system running inside the booth
insights.locator: Kioxia even showed the drive running

insights.claim: The stated industry goal is to push NVMe SSDs into the 100M IOPS range by roughly next year, a 10x jump over the 10M IOPS drives being shown now.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: A stated 10x roadmap within a year means storage-controller, PCIe switching and NAND-interface suppliers face a step-change in demand, not an incremental refresh.
insights.quote: Eventually, the goal by next year or so is to get drives into the 100M IOPS range.
insights.locator: There is a new push in the industry

themes.theme: SLC vs TLC as the performance lever

insights.claim: Kioxia is using XL-FLASH generation 2, a low-latency SLC-class NAND, to reach extreme per-drive IOPS instead of relying on broad TLC parallelism.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: If SLC-class media becomes the standard route to Gen6-class IOPS, NAND mix shifts toward lower-density, higher-value wafers — a margin lever distinct from the capacity glut.
insights.quote: where a drive can achieve high per-device IOPS through SLC rather than relying on broad TLC parallelism

insights.claim: 512-byte access granularity combined with high write endurance positions the GP1 for workloads where latency and sustained rewrite matter more than raw capacity.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Identifies the buyer: latency-bound AI and database tiers, not bulk storage — a segment where price-per-IOPS, not price-per-TB, sets the deal.

insights.claim: The GP1 family spans E3.S and E1.S in 9.5 mm and 15 mm heights, all air-cooled, with cold-plate liquid cooling supported on the E3.S and E1.S 9.5 mm variants.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Dual air/liquid support inside one family lowers the design-win barrier across both legacy air-cooled and new liquid-cooled server chassis.

insights.claim: Supporting both air and cold-plate cooling within one drive family lets a server maker pick the cooling approach that fits its chassis rather than locking in a single scheme.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Cooling flexibility is becoming a competitive spec in storage, mirroring the liquid-cooling transition already underway on the compute side.
insights.locator: Supporting both air and cold-plate cooling

insights.claim: A new ultra-fast storage tier for AI servers is emerging that offloads some traditional DRAM tasks to lower-cost NAND, requiring far higher-performance SSDs to work.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: A structural substitution of NAND for DRAM in AI servers would reprice both memory markets; watch attach rates of high-IOPS SSDs per accelerator node.
insights.quote: While the market is capacity-constrained in general, a new ultra-fast storage tier for AI servers prioritizes performance, offloading some traditional DRAM tasks to lower-cost NAND.

insights.claim: The GP1 supersedes the Kioxia FL6, which used an earlier XL-FLASH generation and only supported PCIe Gen4 — a two-generation interface jump to Gen6.
insights.speaker: Sam Sabinash
insights.so_what: Skipping straight from Gen4 to Gen6 in this product line shows how quickly the fast-tier refresh cycle is compressing for storage vendors.
insights.locator: Previously, we looked at the Kioxia FL6
